summary.text: J.D. Ford is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 5th District. A former fraternity executive and nonprofit professional, he has represented Indiana Senate District 29 since 2018 as the first openly LGBTQ+ member of the General Assembly and is not seeking re-election to the state Senate. His campaign emphasizes affordability, healthcare and care costs.

paragraphs.text: According to his Candidate Connection survey, learned the value of hard work from his father, a union truck driver, and his mother, an assisted living administrator, and was influenced by grandparents who served as local officials.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and criminal justice from the University of Akron (2005) and a master's degree in education from Purdue University (2010).
Worked as senior director of recruitment and expansion for Theta Chi Fraternity, Inc.; Ballotpedia lists his profession as nonprofit professional.
Elected to Indiana Senate District 29 on November 6, 2018, defeating Republican incumbent Mike Delph; took office November 7, 2018, and was re-elected in 2022.
Describes himself as the first, and so far only, openly LGBTQ+ member of the Indiana General Assembly.

Serves on the Indiana Senate's Commerce and Technology, Education and Career Development, Health and Provider Services, Elections, Family & Children Services, Homeland Security and Transportation, Utilities, and Veterans Affairs and the Military committees in the 2025-2026 session; earlier he served as ranking minority member of several committees and vice chair of the Ethics Committee.
